claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength in its simple solid-solution state.
The relatively low hardness and strength are primarily caused by limited lattice distortion.
The relatively low hardness and strength are also caused by a lack of appreciable short-range chemical order.
Limited lattice distortion and weak short-range order permit easier dislocation glide.
Easier dislocation glide gives the alloy high plasticity and machinability.
The simple solid solution produces weaker solid-solution strengthening than chemically segregated or multiphase high-entropy alloys.
The starting material is an as-cast, equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy with a homogeneous single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
The starting solid solution is likely FCC, although it may instead be BCC.
A controlled heat treatment can promote nanoscale short-range order or incipient precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
The degree of lattice distortion and the extent of short-range order or nanoprecipitation mediate dislocation motion.
The as-cast state has minimal atomic-size mismatch and a low density of obstacles to dislocation glide.
Heat-treatment-induced short-range order or fine precipitates increase local lattice distortion and hinder dislocation motion.
Heat treatment will increase hardness, yield strength, deformation resistance, and lattice friction relative to the as-cast baseline.
The strengthening caused by heat treatment will reduce plastic strain.
The predicted strengthening and loss of plasticity will be detectable at room temperature and persist up to 600 °C.
The hypothesis is limited to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi under quasi-static loading from room temperature through 600 °C.
The hypothesis applies only when the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution without secondary phases.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mechanism allow incipient precipitation or fine precipitates as the strengthening mediator, whereas the boundary restricts the hypothesis to a single-phase solid solution with no secondary phases, and the predicted outcome invokes persistence within a maintained homogeneous state.
